hook.convey: one whole stretch from start = 0 to finish = 1; stopping exactly halfway → standing on a real spot → 0 and 1 have no name for it → fractions are numbers that live between 0 and 1

use.hi: Cricket ki pitch socho. Ek stump 0 par, doosra 1 par. Batsman run lene bhaaga aur theek beech mein ruk gaya. Woh pitch ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai, toh us jagah ka bhi ek number hai.
use.en: Picture a cricket pitch. One stump at 0, the other at 1. The batsman sets off for a run and stops right in the middle. He's standing on a real spot, so that spot has a number too.

use.hi: Ghar 0 par, school 1 kilometre par. School bus aadhe raaste mein ruk gayi. Na 0 par, na 1 par, beech mein kahin. Us jagah ka bhi number hota hai.
use.en: Home is at 0, school at 1 kilometre. The school bus stops halfway. Not at 0, not at 1, somewhere in between. That place has a number too.

use.hi: Game mein level ki progress 0 se shuru hoti hai, aur 1 par level khatam. Abhi progress aadhi hui hai. Matlab woh 0 aur 1 ke beech ke ek number par ruki hai.
use.en: In a game a level's progress starts at 0, and at 1 the level is done. Right now it's halfway. So it has stopped at a number between 0 and 1.

explain.convey: 0 and 1 at the ends; one cut exactly in the middle → 2 equal gaps; the middle mark = 1/2 → 1/2 is a number with its own place, between 0 and 1, not at 2

viewCaption.hi: Yahan line ki jagah ek patti hai, do barabar hisson mein, aur ek hissa rangin hai. Rangin hissa patti ke shuru se theek beech tak jaata hai, jaise line par 0 se beech wale mark tak.
viewCaption.en: Here, in place of the line, there is a strip in two equal parts, with one part coloured. The coloured part runs from the start of the strip to exactly the middle, like 0 to the middle mark on the line.

point.hi: Yeh rahi 0 se 1 tak ki line. Theek beech mein ek mark hai, toh line ke 2 barabar gaps ban gaye. Is mark ka naam hai 1/2.
point.en: Here's a line from 0 to 1. There is one mark right in the middle, so the line now has 2 equal gaps. This mark is called 1/2.

pointAlt.hi: Ek roti ko theek beech se kaato toh do barabar hisse milte hain. Line par bhi beech wala mark 0 se 1 ko aise hi do barabar gaps mein baant-ta hai, isliye woh 1/2 hai.
pointAlt.en: Cut a roti right down the middle and you get two equal parts. The middle mark on the line splits 0 to 1 the same way, into two equal gaps, so it is 1/2.

prompt.hi: Batao, 1/3 isi 0 se 1 wali line par aata hai, ya 3 ke paas?
prompt.en: Tell me: does 1/3 come on this same line from 0 to 1, or near 3?

accept: woh isi line par aata hai

simpler.hi: 1/3 ka neeche wala number 3 batata hai ki ek poore ko 3 barabar gaps mein kaatna hai. Ab socho, board par woh ek poora kahan se kahan tak hai.
simpler.en: The bottom number of 1/3, the 3, says to cut one whole into 3 equal gaps. Now think where that one whole runs on the board.

why.hi: neeche wala number 3 matlab 0 se 1 ke 3 barabar gaps, aur pehla gap isi line par khatam hota hai
why.en: the bottom number 3 means 3 equal gaps from 0 to 1, and the first gap ends right on this line

whyAlt.hi: 1/3 poore 1 se chhota hai, toh woh 0 aur 1 ke beech hi aata hai, 3 ke paas kabhi nahi
whyAlt.en: 1/3 is smaller than one whole, so it comes between 0 and 1, never near 3

viewCaption.hi: Yahan do barabar lambi pattiyaan hain: pehli do barabar hisson mein, ek hissa rangin, aur doosri teen barabar hisson mein, abhi bina rang ke.
viewCaption.en: Here are two strips of the same length: the first in two equal parts with one coloured, and the second in three equal parts, not coloured yet.

simpler.hi: 0 se beech wale mark tak ek gap, aur wahan se 1 tak ek aur: dono gap ek jitne lambe. Do mein se pehla gap, isliye 1/2.
simpler.en: From 0 to the middle mark is one gap, and from there to 1 another: both gaps the same length. The first of two gaps, so 1/2.

explain.convey: same 0 to 1, now 6 marks inside → 7 equal gaps (gaps = marks inside + 1); bottom number = number of equal gaps in 0 to 1; first mark from 0 = end of 1 gap = 1/7; the name comes from gaps, not marks

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti saat barabar hisson mein hai, aur uska pehla hissa rangin hai, 1/7. Patti par hisson ke beech chhe marks hain, par hisse saat.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is in seven equal parts, and its first part is coloured, 1/7. The strip has six marks between its parts, but seven parts.

point.hi: Wahi 0 se 1 ki line, par ab line ke upar 6 marks hain. Marks mat gino, gaps gino: 7 barabar gaps. Toh 0 ke baad pehla mark hai 1/7.
point.en: Same line from 0 to 1, but now there are 6 marks above the line. Don't count the marks, count the gaps: 7 equal gaps. So the first mark after 0 is 1/7.

pointAlt.hi: 0 se chalo: har mark se pehle ek gap aata hai, toh 6 marks ke 6 gaps, aur aakhri mark ke baad 1 tak ek gap aur. Isliye 6 marks ke saath 7 gaps hain, aur 0 ke baad wala pehla mark 1/7 hai.
pointAlt.en: Walk from 0: there is a gap before each mark, so 6 marks give 6 gaps, and one more gap after the last mark up to 1. That's why 6 marks come with 7 gaps, and the first mark after 0 is 1/7.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche dekho. Wahan 0 aur 1 ke beech 7 marks hain, sab barabar doori par. Line ke neeche kitne barabar gaps bane hain?
prompt.en: Look below the line. There are 7 marks between 0 and 1, all evenly spaced. How many equal gaps are there below the line?

why.hi: beech ke marks se gaps hamesha ek zyada, toh 7 marks ke 8 gaps
why.en: there's always one more gap than marks in between, so 7 marks make 8 gaps

whyAlt.hi: line ke neeche wale marks par chalkar gino: 0 se pehle mark tak ek gap, phir 7 marks mein se har mark ke baad ek gap, toh 1 + 7 = 8 gaps
whyAlt.en: walk along the marks below the line: one gap from 0 to the first mark, then one gap after each of the 7 marks, so 1 + 7 = 8 gaps

simpler.hi: Line ke neeche marks ke beech ki khaali jagah gino, aur 0 ke baad wali aur 1 se pehle wali jagah bhi mat chhodna.
simpler.en: Below the line, count the empty spaces between the marks, and don't leave out the space after 0 and the space before 1.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti saat barabar hisson mein hai, uska pehla hissa rangin. Doosri patti utni hi lambi hai aur abhi bina rang ke; uske hisse line ke neeche wale marks se bante hain.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is in seven equal parts, its first part coloured. The second strip is just as long and not coloured yet; its parts are made by the marks below the line.

simpler.hi: Line ke upar 6 marks the aur 7 gaps. Gap marks ke beech bhi hote hain aur dono siron par bhi, isliye gaps hamesha marks se ek zyada.
simpler.en: Above the line there were 6 marks and 7 gaps. Gaps sit between the marks and at both ends too, so there is always one more gap than marks.

explain.convey: the same 0 to 1 in 8 equal gaps → more gaps than the 7 before → each gap smaller; 1/8 = first mark, right next to 0; 1/2 still the middle mark (4 of the 8 gaps); more equal gaps in the same whole → each gap shorter → 1/8 sits closer to 0 than 1/7 and 1/2

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti aath barabar hisson mein hai, aur uska ek rangin hissa 1/8 hai; doosri patti do hisson mein hai, aur uska rangin hissa aadha. Dono rangin hisson ki lambai milaakar dekho.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is in eight equal parts, and its one coloured part is 1/8; the second strip is in two parts, and its coloured part is a half. Compare the lengths of the two coloured parts.

point.hi: Ab wahi 0 se 1, par line par 8 barabar gaps hain. Pehle 7 gaps the, ab zyada hain, toh har gap pehle se chhota hai. Pehla mark 1/8 hai, 0 se theek ek gap door.
point.en: Now the same 0 to 1, but the line has 8 equal gaps. Before there were 7 gaps; now there are more, so each gap is smaller than before. The first mark is 1/8, exactly one gap from 0.

pointAlt.hi: Ek chocolate ko 8 barabar hisson mein todo, toh har hissa 7 hisson wale se patla hota hai. Line par bhi 8 barabar gaps mein har gap chhota hai, isliye pehla mark, 1/8, 1/7 se pehle aata hai.
pointAlt.en: Break a chocolate into 8 equal parts and each part is thinner than with 7 parts. On the line too, with 8 equal gaps each gap is short, so the first mark, 1/8, comes before 1/7.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche wahi 0 se 1, 10 barabar gaps mein kata hai. 0 ke zyada paas kaun rukega: 1/8 ya 1/10?
prompt.en: Below the line, the same 0 to 1 is cut into 10 equal gaps. Which stops closer to 0: 1/8 or 1/10?

why.hi: 10 gaps wala har gap 8 gaps wale se chhota hai, isliye 1/10 pehle ruk jaata hai, 0 ke paas
why.en: a gap out of 10 is smaller than a gap out of 8, so 1/10 stops sooner, nearer 0

whyAlt.hi: ek hi deewar par do seedhiyaan socho, ek mein 8 barabar paydaan aur ek mein 10: 10 wali seedhi ka pehla paydaan zameen ke zyada paas hota hai, waise hi line par 1/10 pehle rukta hai, 0 ke zyada paas
whyAlt.en: picture two ladders against the same wall, one with 8 equal steps and one with 10: the 10-step ladder's first step is nearer the ground, and in the same way 1/10 stops first on the line, nearer 0

simpler.hi: Line ke upar aur neeche ka pehla gap ungli se naapo, aur dekho kaunsa gap chhota hai.
simpler.en: Measure the first gap above the line and the first gap below it with your finger, and see which gap is shorter.

viewCaption.hi: Dhyan pehle hisse par rakho: pehli patti aath barabar hisson mein hai aur uska pehla hissa rangin hai, doosri utni hi lambi patti das barabar hisson mein. Dono pattiyon ka baayan kinaara line ka 0 hai.
viewCaption.en: Keep your eye on the first part: the first strip is in eight equal parts with its first part coloured, and the second strip, just as long, is in ten equal parts. The left end of both strips is the line's 0.

simpler.hi: Line ke 8 barabar gaps ek-ek karke gino. Pehla mark pehle gap ke khatam hote hi aata hai.
simpler.en: Count the line's 8 equal gaps one by one. The first mark comes as soon as the first gap ends.

problem.hi: Ghar 0 par hai aur school 1 kilometre par. Beech raaste mein 3 bijli ke khambe barabar doori par khade hain. Pehla khamba ghar se kitne kilometre door hai?
problem.en: Home is at 0 and school is at 1 kilometre. Along the road between them stand 3 electric poles, evenly spaced. How many kilometres from home is the first pole?

problemAlt.hi: Socho tum ghar se school ja rahe ho, raasta 1 kilometre ka. Raaste mein 3 bijli ke khambe aise lage hain ki ghar, teeno khambe aur school, sab ek-doosre se barabar doori par hain. Pehla khamba kitni door milega, yahi nikalna hai.
problemAlt.en: Picture going from home to school, a 1 kilometre road. Along it stand 3 electric poles, placed so that home, the three poles and school are all the same distance apart. How far away the first pole is, is what we find.

simpler.hi: Pehle chhota socho: beech mein sirf 1 khamba hota, toh woh theek aadhe raaste par, 1/2 kilometre par hota. Ab 3 khambe hain, toh pehle yeh dekho ki woh raaste ko kitne barabar gaps mein baant-te hain.
simpler.en: Start smaller: with just 1 pole in between, it would stand exactly halfway, at 1/2 kilometre. Now there are 3 poles, so first see how many equal gaps they cut the road into.

givens.hi: poora raasta 1 kilometre ka, aur beech mein 3 khambe
givens.en: a 1 kilometre road with 3 poles in between

find.hi: pehle khambe ki doori, kilometre mein
find.en: how far the first pole is, in kilometres

do.hi: Ek line kheencho, ghar 0 par aur school 1 par
do.en: Draw a line with home at 0 and school at 1

why.hi: ghar se school tak ka poora raasta hi humara ek poora hai
why.en: the whole road from home to school is our one whole

simpler.hi: Agar school aur door hota, toh line aur lambi kheenchte. Yahan raasta theek 1 kilometre ka hai, isliye line 0 se 1 tak, aur yahi humara ek poora hai.
simpler.en: If school were further away, we'd draw a longer line. Here the road is exactly 1 kilometre, so the line runs 0 to 1, and that is our one whole.

do.hi: Khambe mat gino, unke beech ke gaps gino
do.en: Don't count the poles, count the gaps between them

why.hi: beech mein jitne marks hon, gaps hamesha usse ek zyada
why.en: there is always one more gap than marks in between

simpler.hi: Ghar se pehle khambe tak ek gap, phir khambe se khamba, aur aakhri khambe se school tak ek. 3 khambe, 4 gaps.
simpler.en: Home to the first pole is one gap, then pole to pole, then the last pole to school. 3 poles, 4 gaps.

prompt.hi: Raasta 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai, aur pehla khamba ghar se bas ek gap door hai. Woh kitne kilometre par hai?
prompt.en: The road is in 4 equal gaps, and the first pole is just one gap from home. At how many kilometres is it?

reask.hi: 1 kilometre ka raasta 4 barabar gaps mein ho, toh ghar se ek gap door pehla khamba kitne kilometre par hai?
reask.en: If a 1 kilometre road is in 4 equal gaps, how many kilometres from home is the first pole, one gap along?

why.hi: raasta 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai aur pehla khamba theek ek gap par hai
why.en: the road is in 4 equal gaps and the first pole stands exactly one gap along

whyAlt.hi: 4 barabar gaps milkar poora 1 kilometre banate hain, toh ek gap 1 kilometre ka ek chauthai hai, yaani 1/4 kilometre
whyAlt.en: 4 equal gaps make the whole 1 kilometre, so one gap is one quarter of the kilometre, that is 1/4 kilometre

simpler.hi: Poora raasta 1 kilometre ka hai, aur woh 4 barabar gaps mein bata hai. Ek gap 1 kilometre ka kaunsa fraction hai, bas yahi socho.
simpler.en: The whole road is 1 kilometre, cut into 4 equal gaps. Just think what fraction of 1 kilometre one gap is.

answer.hi: pehla khamba ghar se 1/4 kilometre door hai
answer.en: the first pole is 1/4 kilometre from home

why.hi: 4 barabar gaps mein har gap 1/4 kilometre ka hai, aur pehla khamba 0 se theek ek gap par khada hai
why.en: with 4 equal gaps each gap is 1/4 kilometre, and the first pole stands exactly one gap from 0

viewCaption.hi: Is patti ko raasta samjho: baayan kinaara ghar, daayan kinaara school, aur hisson ke beech ke teen marks teen khambe. Rangin hissa ghar se pehle khambe tak ka raasta hai.
viewCaption.en: Take this strip as the road: the left end is home, the right end is school, and the three marks between the parts are the three poles. The coloured part is the road from home to the first pole.

prompt.hi: Is line par 0 aur 1 ke beech 10 marks hain, barabar doori par. 0 ke baad pehla mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: This line has 10 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1. What fraction is the first mark after 0?

did.hi: 10 marks se bane gaps gine aur pehle mark ka naam rakha
did.en: counted the gaps 10 marks make and named the first mark

viewCaption.hi: Yeh patti barabar hisson mein kati hai, aur sirf pehla hissa rangin hai. Hisson ke beech ke marks wahi hain jo line par 0 aur 1 ke beech the; ab baayein kinaare se daayein kinaare tak saare hisse gino.
viewCaption.en: This strip is cut into equal parts, and only the first part is coloured. The marks between the parts are the ones that sat between 0 and 1 on the line; now count every part, from the left end to the right end.

why.hi: 10 marks se line ke 11 barabar gaps bante hain, aur pehla mark ek gap par hai, yaani 1/11
why.en: 10 marks make 11 equal gaps, and the first mark is one gap along, at 1/11

whyAlt.hi: chhota karke dekho: 1 mark ho toh 2 gaps, 2 marks ho toh 3 gaps; isi tarah 10 marks ke 11 gaps, toh pehla mark 1/11
whyAlt.en: try it smaller: 1 mark gives 2 gaps, 2 marks give 3 gaps; the same way 10 marks give 11 gaps, so the first mark is 1/11

simpler.hi: Marks chhodo, gaps gino. 0 se 1 ki line par 10 marks se jitne gaps bane, wahi neeche wala number hai.
simpler.en: Forget the marks, count the gaps. On a line from 0 to 1, however many gaps the 10 marks make, that's the bottom number.

prompt.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 1/11 line par 1/4 ke baad aata hai, kyunki 11, 4 se bada hai. {friend} sahi hai ya galat?
prompt.en: {friend} says 1/11 comes after 1/4 on the line, because 11 is bigger than 4. Is {friend} right or wrong?

reask.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 1/11 line par 1/4 ke baad aata hai: yeh sahi hai ya galat?
reask.en: {friend} says 1/11 comes after 1/4 on the line: is that right or wrong?

did.hi: 1/11 aur 1/4 ke gap milaakar ek galat daava pakda
did.en: compared the gaps of 1/11 and 1/4 and caught a wrong claim

viewCaption.hi: Do barabar lambi pattiyaan hain, pehli chaar barabar hisson mein aur doosri gyarah mein. Dono pattiyon ka pehla hissa, baayein kinaare se, dhyan se dekho.
viewCaption.en: There are two strips of the same length, the first in four equal parts and the second in eleven. Look closely at the first part of each strip, from the left end.

why.hi: 11 barabar gaps mein har gap 4 wale gap se chhota hai, isliye 1/11 pehle rukta hai; {friend} galat hai
why.en: with 11 equal gaps each gap is smaller than with 4, so 1/11 stops sooner; {friend} is wrong

whyAlt.hi: ek pizza 11 logon mein bate toh har ek ko 4 logon wale se chhota hissa milta hai; 1/11 chhota hai, isliye line par 1/4 se pehle aata hai, aur {friend} galat hai
whyAlt.en: share a pizza among 11 and each gets a smaller part than among 4; 1/11 is smaller, so on the line it comes before 1/4, and {friend} is wrong

simpler.hi: Socho ek roti 4 logon mein bati, ya 11 logon mein: 11 logon mein har hissa chhota hai. Line par bhi jiska gap chhota, woh pehle rukta hai.
simpler.en: Imagine one roti shared among 4, or among 11: among 11 each part is smaller. On the line too, the one with the smaller gap stops sooner.

prompt.hi: Line 0 se 1 tak 9 barabar gaps mein hai. Kuch log sochte hain ki line par 1/9 ki koi jagah nahi hoti. 1/9 ki jagah 0 ke baad kaunsa mark hai?
prompt.en: The line from 0 to 1 is in 9 equal gaps. Some people think 1/9 has no place on a line. Which mark after 0 is the place of 1/9?

did.hi: 9 gaps wali line par 1/9 ki jagah dhoondhi
did.en: found where 1/9 sits on a line of 9 gaps

viewCaption.hi: Board par 0 se 1 tak ki line hai, nau barabar gaps mein, aur beech mein aath marks. 0 se shuru karke gaps ek-ek karke dekho.
viewCaption.en: The board shows a line from 0 to 1, in nine equal gaps, with eight marks in between. Start at 0 and look at the gaps one by one.

why.hi: 1/9 matlab 9 barabar gaps mein se 1 gap, toh 1/9 ki jagah 0 se ek gap par, pehle mark par hai
why.en: 1/9 means 1 gap out of 9 equal gaps, so 1/9 sits one gap from 0, at the first mark

whyAlt.hi: jaise 7 gaps wali line par 0 ke baad pehla mark 1/7 tha, waise hi 9 gaps wali line par pehla mark 1/9 hai; line par har fraction ki apni jagah hai
whyAlt.en: just as on the line of 7 gaps the first mark after 0 was 1/7, on a line of 9 gaps the first mark is 1/9; every fraction has its own place on the line

simpler.hi: 1/9 ka neeche wala number 9 batata hai ki line 9 barabar gaps mein kati hai. Ab socho, 0 se ek gap chalkar kahan pahunchte hain.
simpler.en: The bottom number of 1/9, the 9, says the line is cut into 9 equal gaps. Now think where one gap from 0 takes you.

ladder.why: den 2: one cut, gaps obvious → fraction as a place on the road; same den as e1
den 4 (halves halved, as in e2 and the worked example) → 2nd mark = 2/4 → same spot as 1/2; gap-value thinking, not mark counting
den 5 given only as marks (4 inside) → must convert marks to gaps; error-spot on the count-marks trap
den 6 again but given as 5 inside marks → contrasts with rl-o1 (same den, gaps given) → explain why the label is wrong

remediation.move: ribbon at a tailor's shop, 0 to 1 m, one line cut in 7 on top and 12 below; marks = chalk marks, the ribbon between marks = gaps (never hisse); marks inside + 1 = gaps; a mark's name comes from counting gaps, not marks; top: 6 marks → 7 gaps → first mark at 1/7 m; then below: first mark at 1/12 m → 12 gaps → 11 marks (the trap says 12)

say.hi: Darzi ka ribbon socho, 0 se 1 metre. Line ke upar 6 chalk ke marks hain, aur ribbon ke 7 barabar gap. Pehla mark pehle gap ke end par hai, yaani 1/7 metre. Naam gap ginkar milta hai, marks ginkar nahi.
say.en: Picture a tailor's ribbon, 0 to 1 metre. Above the line there are 6 chalk marks, and the ribbon makes 7 equal gaps. The first mark ends the first gap, at 1/7 metre. The name comes from counting gaps, not marks.

simpler.hi: Line ke upar ungli 0 se 1 tak sarkao aur har khaali jagah par ek gino. Ginti chalk marks se ek zyada aati hai.
simpler.en: Slide your finger above the line from 0 to 1 and count one for each empty space. The count comes out one more than the chalk marks.

sayAlt.hi: Do deewaron ke beech kapde sukhane ki rassi par 6 clip socho: pehli deewar se pehle clip tak ek khaali jagah, clipon ke beech 5, aur aakhri clip se deewar tak ek, kul 7. Chalk ke 6 marks bhi aise hi 7 gap banate hain.
sayAlt.en: Picture a clothesline between two walls with 6 pegs: one space from the first wall to the first peg, 5 between the pegs, and one from the last peg to the wall, 7 in all. The 6 chalk marks make 7 gaps the same way.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti darzi ka ribbon hai: saat barabar hisse, aur pehla hissa rangin, yaani 1/7 metre. Hisson ke beech ke marks hi chalk ke marks hain.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is the tailor's ribbon: seven equal parts, with the first part coloured, that is 1/7 metre. The marks between the parts are the chalk marks.

prompt.hi: Ribbon par line ke neeche pehla chalk mark 1/12 metre par hai. Line ke neeche kitne chalk ke marks hain?
prompt.en: On the ribbon, below the line, the first chalk mark is at 1/12 metre. How many chalk marks are there below the line?

reask.hi: Pehla chalk mark 1/12 metre par ho, toh ribbon par line ke neeche kitne chalk ke marks hain?
reask.en: If the first chalk mark is at 1/12 metre, how many chalk marks are there below the line on the ribbon?

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti ribbon ke saat barabar hisse dikhati hai, pehla rangin. Doosri patti abhi poori hai, bina kisi mark ke, uske chalk ke marks tumhe sochne hain.
viewCaption.en: The first strip shows the ribbon's seven equal parts, the first one coloured. The second strip is still whole, with no mark on it; its chalk marks are for you to work out.

why.hi: 1/12 metre matlab ribbon ke 12 barabar gap, aur 12 gap ke beech 11 marks hote hain
why.en: 1/12 metre means the ribbon is in 12 equal gaps, and 12 gaps have 11 marks between them

whyAlt.hi: chhote numbers se socho: 2 gap ke beech 1 mark hota hai, 3 gap ke beech 2; har baar marks gap se ek kam, toh 12 gap ke beech 11 marks
whyAlt.en: think with small numbers: 2 gaps have 1 mark between them, 3 gaps have 2; marks are always one fewer than gaps, so 12 gaps have 11 marks

simpler.hi: Line ke neeche wale gap socho: marks gap ke beech hote hain, isliye marks hamesha gap se ek kam.
simpler.en: Think of the ribbon's gaps below the line: the marks sit between the gaps, so there is always one mark fewer than gaps.

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (one 0-to-1 line, fifths on top, sevenths below, 1/5 marked), naming none of its numbers: both lines are the same whole; a bigger bottom number shares the same whole into more gaps, so each gap is smaller → bigger bottom number = smaller gap; then the child places 1/7: between 0 and 1/5, not after it

say.hi: Board par ek line hai: line ke dono taraf ke gap 0 se 1 ka wahi ek poora baant-te hain. Fraction ka neeche wala number jitna bada, utne zyada barabar gaps, aur har gap utna chhota. Bada number matlab bada gap nahi.
say.en: The board has one line: the gaps on both sides of it share out the same whole, 0 to 1. The bigger a fraction's bottom number, the more equal gaps, and the smaller each gap. A bigger number does not mean a bigger gap.

simpler.hi: Dono taraf wahi 0 se 1 hai. Jis taraf gap zyada hain, wahan har gap ko kam jagah milti hai.
simpler.en: Both sides hold the same 0 to 1. On the side with more gaps, each gap gets less room.

sayAlt.hi: Ek hi laddu socho: 2 bachchon mein baanto toh har ek ko bada hissa milta hai, 10 bachchon mein baanto toh chhota. 1/10 ka 10 baantne walon ki ginti jaisa hai: woh jitna bada, har gap utna chhota.
sayAlt.en: Think of one laddoo: share it between 2 children and each gets a big part, among 10 and each gets a small one. The 10 of 1/10 is like the number of children sharing: the bigger it is, the smaller each gap.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche 7 gaps hain, aur line ke upar pehla mark 1/5 hai. 1/7 kahaan aayega: 0 aur 1/5 ke beech, ya baad mein?
prompt.en: Below the line, 7 gaps; above it, the first mark is 1/5. Where does 1/7 go: between 0 and 1/5, or after?

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti ka pehla hissa rangin hai, 1/5. Doosri patti utni hi lambi hai par saat barabar hisson mein, uska pehla hissa bhi baayein kinaare se dekho.
viewCaption.en: The first part of the first strip is coloured, 1/5. The second strip is just as long but in seven equal parts; look at its first part from the left end too.

why.hi: 7 gaps wala har gap 5 gaps wale se chhota hai, isliye 1/7, 0 aur 1/5 ke beech rukta hai
why.en: a gap out of 7 is smaller than a gap out of 5, so 1/7 stops between 0 and 1/5

whyAlt.hi: 5 gap milkar 0 se 1 bharte hain, aur 7 gap ko bhi wahi 0 se 1 bharna hai, toh 7 waala har gap chhota hoga; isliye 1/7 pehle aata hai, 0 aur 1/5 ke beech
whyAlt.en: 5 gaps fill 0 to 1, and 7 gaps must fill the same 0 to 1, so each of the 7 is shorter; that's why 1/7 comes first, between 0 and 1/5

simpler.hi: 1/7 wala gap 1/5 wale gap se chhota hai. Chhota gap pehle khatam ho jaata hai.
simpler.en: A 1/7 gap is shorter than a 1/5 gap. A shorter gap ends sooner.

remediation.move: road from home (0) to the chai stall (1 km), one line in 7 equal gaps on top; a toy walks from home and stops at the first mark → it stands on one real spot of the road → that spot has one number, 1/7 km; then the same road in 6 gaps below: the toy stops at the first mark below → that spot is one number too, 1/6 km (the trap says 1 and 6); no top number above 1 yet (taught in s2)

say.hi: Ghar 0 par, chai ki dukaan 1 kilometre par, aur line ke upar sadak 7 barabar gaps mein bati hai. Ek chaabi wala khilona pehle mark par ruka. Woh sadak ki ek pakki jagah par khada hai, uska number 1/7 kilometre hai.
say.en: Home is at 0, the chai stall at 1 kilometre, and above the line the road is in 7 equal gaps. A wind-up toy stops at the first mark. It stands on one real spot of the road, and its number is 1/7 kilometre.

simpler.hi: Ghar se khilone tak sadak ka bas ek gap hai, aur poori sadak mein aise 7 gap hain. Khilone ki jagah ka naam yahi ginti hai.
simpler.en: From home to the toy is just one gap of the road, and the whole road has 7 such gaps. The toy's spot is named by this count.

sayAlt.hi: Number se jagah tak chalo: 1/7 kilometre sadak par ek hi jagah hai, line ke upar pehla mark. Ek jagah ka ek hi naam hota hai, isliye 1/7 ek number hai, do alag number nahi.
sayAlt.en: Go from the number to the spot: 1/7 kilometre is one place on the road, the first mark above the line. One place has one name, so 1/7 is one number, not two separate numbers.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti sadak hai, ghar se chai ki dukaan tak: saat barabar hisse, aur rangin hissa wahan tak jahan khilona ruka, 1/7 kilometre. Doosri patti wahi sadak hai, chhe barabar hisson mein.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is the road from home to the chai stall: seven equal parts, and the coloured part goes as far as where the toy stopped, 1/7 kilometre. The second strip is the same road, in six equal parts.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche wahi sadak 6 barabar gaps mein hai, aur khilona pehle mark par ruka: woh 0 se kitne kilometre par hai?
prompt.en: Below the line the same road is in 6 equal gaps, and the toy stops at the first mark: how many kilometres from 0 is it?

viewCaption.hi: Dono pattiyaan ek hi sadak hain, ghar se chai ki dukaan tak. Pehli mein pehla hissa rangin hai, aur doosri chhe barabar hisson mein bati hai, abhi bina rang ke.
viewCaption.en: Both strips are the same road, from home to the chai stall. The first has its first part coloured, and the second is in six equal parts, not coloured yet.

why.hi: line ke neeche sadak 6 barabar gaps mein hai, aur pehla mark 0 se ek gap par, yaani 1/6 kilometre
why.en: below the line the road is in 6 equal gaps and the first mark is one gap from 0, at 1/6 kilometre

whyAlt.hi: khilona 6 barabar gaps wali sadak par 0 se bas ek gap chala; '6 mein se 1 gap' ko ek number mein bolte hain 1/6 kilometre
whyAlt.en: the toy walked just one gap from 0 on a road of 6 equal gaps; '1 gap out of 6' said as one number is 1/6 kilometre

simpler.hi: Line ke neeche bhi wahi sadak hai, bas 6 barabar gaps mein. Ek gap poore kilometre ka kaunsa fraction hai, yahi socho.
simpler.en: Below the line is the same road, just in 6 equal gaps. Just think what fraction of the whole kilometre one gap is.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab 0 se ek se zyada gap chalenge, aur fraction ka upar wala number batayega kitne.
bridgeToNext.en: Next we'll move more than one gap from 0, and a fraction's top number will tell us how many.

simpler.hi: Ab upar wala number batayega ki 0 se kitne gap chalne hain.
simpler.en: Now the top number says how many gaps to move from 0.

covered.hi: Aaj ki baat yeh thi ki 0 aur 1 ke beech ke har fraction ki line par ek pakki jagah hoti hai, aur uska naam marks se nahi, barabar gaps ginkar milta hai.
covered.en: Today was about each fraction between 0 and 1 having its own place on the line, with its name coming from counting the equal gaps, not the marks.

hook.convey: same 0-to-1 stretch cut into equal stretches; the stop is not the first mark but several stretches on → its name needs two facts: how many equal stretches make the whole (bottom), how many are covered from 0 (top)

use.hi: Cricket pitch ko 4 barabar gaps mein baanto. Batsman 0 wale stump se bhaaga aur 3 gap paar karke ruka. Uski jagah batane ke liye do cheezein chahiye: pitch ke kitne gaps hain, aur usne kitne paar kiye.
use.en: Split a cricket pitch into 4 equal gaps. The batsman runs from the stump at 0 and stops after 3 gaps. To name his spot we need two things: how many gaps the pitch has, and how many he crossed.

use.hi: Game ki loading 0 se 1 tak bharti hai, 5 barabar gaps mein. Abhi loading 0 se 2 gap tak bhari hai. Kitni bhari, yeh batane ke liye do number chahiye, ek neeche wala number aur ek upar wala number.
use.en: A game's loading fills from 0 to 1, in 5 equal gaps. Right now it has loaded 2 gaps from 0. To say how much has loaded, we need two numbers, a bottom number and a top number.

explain.convey: thirds: bottom 3 → 0 to 1 in 3 equal gaps; top 2 → 2 hops of 1/3 from 0; landing mark = 2/3 → one point, one number, not 2 and 3 separately

viewCaption.hi: Yeh patti teen barabar hisson mein hai, aur pehle do hisse rangin hain, 2/3. Rang baayein kinaare se shuru hota hai, jaise line par 0 se gap chalna.
viewCaption.en: This strip is in three equal parts, and the first two parts are coloured, 2/3. The colour starts from the left end, like walking gaps from 0 on the line.

point.hi: Is baar line 3 barabar gaps mein kati hai, har gap 1/3. 0 se 2 gap chalo, ek, do, aur hum 2/3 par aa gaye. 2/3 ek hi jagah hai, ek hi number.
point.en: This time the line is cut into 3 equal gaps, each gap 1/3. Move 2 gaps from 0, one, two, and we're at 2/3. 2/3 is one place, one number.

pointAlt.hi: Yahi baat doosre sire se: 2/3 wala mark 0 se 2 gap door hai aur 1 se sirf 1 gap. Line ke 3 gaps mein se 2 uske peeche hain, isliye uska naam 2/3 hai.
pointAlt.en: The same thing from the other end: the 2/3 mark is 2 gaps from 0 and just 1 gap from 1. Of the line's 3 gaps, 2 are behind it, which is why it's called 2/3.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche 8 barabar gaps hain. 0 se 5 gap chalo. Kis fraction par pahunchoge?
prompt.en: Below the line there are 8 equal gaps. Move 5 gaps from 0. Which fraction do you land on?

reask.hi: Line ke neeche wale 8 barabar gaps par 0 se 5 gap chalkar kis fraction par pahunchoge?
reask.en: On the 8 equal gaps below the line, which fraction do you reach after moving 5 gaps from 0?

why.hi: har gap 1/8 ka, aur aise 5 gap mile toh 5/8
why.en: each gap is 1/8, and 5 of them make 5/8

whyAlt.hi: 8 barabar hisson wali chocolate mein se 5 hisse lo toh 8 mein se 5, yaani 5/8; line par bhi 8 mein se 5 gap
whyAlt.en: take 5 parts of a chocolate in 8 equal parts: 5 out of 8, that is 5/8; on the line it's 5 gaps out of 8

simpler.hi: Line ke neeche 0 se ek-ek gap chalo aur paanch tak gino. Phir dekho, poore 1 tak aise kitne gap hain.
simpler.en: Below the line, move one gap at a time from 0 and count to five. Then see how many such gaps there are all the way to 1.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti mein teen mein se do hisse rangin hain. Doosri patti aath barabar hisson mein hai, bina rang ke, aur uske hisse bhi baayein kinaare se ek-ek karke gine jaate hain.
viewCaption.en: In the first strip two of the three parts are coloured. The second strip is in eight equal parts, not coloured, and its parts are counted one by one from the left end too.

simpler.hi: 2/3 ko '3 mein se 2' padho: line jitne hisson mein kati, woh 3; tum jitne chale, woh 2.
simpler.en: Read 2/3 as '2 out of 3': the line is cut into 3, and you moved 2.

explain.convey: still thirds: 3 hops of 1/3 → every gap used → land exactly on 1 → 3/3 = 1; top < bottom → stop before 1; top = bottom → reach 1

viewCaption.hi: Is patti ke teeno barabar hisse rangin hain, toh poori patti bhar gayi. Koi hissa khaali nahi bacha.
viewCaption.en: All three equal parts of this strip are coloured, so the whole strip is filled. No part is left empty.

point.hi: Line 3 barabar gaps mein bati hai. 0 se teen gap chalo toh theek 1 aata hai, isliye wahan 3/3 = 1. Teeno gap milkar 0 se 1 tak ki poori line bhar dete hain.
point.en: The line is cut into 3 equal gaps. Walk three gaps from 0 and you land exactly on 1, so there 3/3 = 1. The three gaps together fill the whole line from 0 to 1.

pointAlt.hi: Pizza ke 3 barabar hisse hon aur teeno le lo, toh poora pizza aa gaya: 3/3 ek poora hai. Line par bhi 3 mein se 3 gap chalkar hum poore 1 par hote hain.
pointAlt.en: If a pizza has 3 equal parts and you take all three, you have the whole pizza: 3/3 is one whole. On the line too, 3 gaps out of 3 put us on the whole 1.

prompt.hi: 1/5 wale gaps dekho. 0 se theek 1 tak pahunchne ke liye aise kitne gap chalne honge?
prompt.en: Look at the gaps of 1/5. How many of them do you move to get from 0 to exactly 1?

reask.hi: Har gap 1/5 ka ho, toh 0 se theek 1 tak kitne gap chalne honge?
reask.en: If each gap is 1/5, how many gaps from 0 to exactly 1?

why.hi: 1/5 ke 5 gap milkar 5/5 banate hain, aur 5/5 = 1
why.en: 5 gaps of 1/5 make 5/5, and 5/5 = 1

whyAlt.hi: ulta socho: 4 gap chalkar tum 1 se theek ek gap pehle ho; 1 par pahunchne ke liye ek gap aur, yaani kul paanch
whyAlt.en: think back from it: 4 gaps leave you exactly one gap short of 1; one more gap reaches 1, so five in all

simpler.hi: 1/5 wale gaps par 0 se chalna shuru karo, aur har gap par ungli rakh kar gino, jab tak 1 na aa jaaye.
simpler.en: Start at 0 on the gaps of 1/5, and count with a finger on each gap until you reach 1.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti teen barabar hisson mein hai; doosri utni hi lambi hai, par uspar abhi koi mark nahi. Doosri poori patti 0 se 1 tak ka ek poora hai.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is in three equal parts; the second is just as long but has no mark on it yet. The whole second strip is one whole, from 0 to 1.

simpler.hi: 3 barabar gaps wali line par teeno gap chalo toh 1 aata hai. Ek bhi gap baaki nahi bachta, isliye chalna theek 1 par rukta hai.
simpler.en: On a line of 3 equal gaps, move all three and you reach 1. Not one gap is left over, so the walk stops exactly at 1.

explain.convey: each third cut in 2 → 6 equal gaps; the middle = half of the 6 gaps = 3 gaps → 3/6 = 1/2; fewer than half the gaps (2/6) → before the middle; more than half (5/6) → after the middle

viewCaption.hi: Teen ek jaisi pattiyaan hain, har ek chhe barabar hisson mein. Pehli mein do hisse rangin, doosri mein teen, aur teesri mein paanch, aur doosri ka rang theek aadhi patti tak hai.
viewCaption.en: There are three identical strips, each in six equal parts. The first has two parts coloured, the second three, and the third five, and the second one's colour reaches exactly half the strip.

point.hi: Ab line ke 6 barabar gaps hain. Theek beech ka mark 3/6 hai, aur 3, 6 ka aadha hai, toh 3/6 = 1/2. 2/6 beech se pehle aata hai, 5/6 beech ke baad.
point.en: Now the line has 6 equal gaps. The mark right in the middle is 3/6, and 3 is half of 6, so 3/6 = 1/2. 2/6 comes before the middle, 5/6 after it.

pointAlt.hi: Roti ke 6 barabar hisse socho: 3 hisse le lo toh theek aadhi roti hai, isliye 3/6 = 1/2 beech mein hai. 2 hisse aadhi se kam hain, toh 2/6 beech se pehle, aur 5 hisse aadhi se zyada, toh 5/6 beech ke baad.
pointAlt.en: Think of a roti in 6 equal parts: take 3 and you have exactly half, so 3/6 = 1/2 is the middle. 2 parts are less than half, so 2/6 comes before the middle, and 5 parts are more than half, so 5/6 after it.

prompt.hi: Isi line par 4/6 kahaan aayega: beech se pehle, ya beech ke baad?
prompt.en: On this same line, where does 4/6 go: before the middle, or after it?

why.hi: beech 3/6 par hai, aur upar wala number 4 usse ek zyada hai, toh ek gap aage, beech ke baad
why.en: the middle is at 3/6, and a top number of 4 is one more, so one gap on, after the middle

whyAlt.hi: 6 mein se 4 gap aadhe se zyada hain, kyunki 6 ka aadha 3 hai; aadhe se zyada wala fraction beech ke baad aata hai
whyAlt.en: 4 gaps out of 6 is more than half, since half of 6 is 3; a fraction past half comes after the middle

simpler.hi: Beech wale mark 3/6 se shuru karo. 4/6 tak pahunchne ke liye kis taraf ek gap chalna padega, woh dekho.
simpler.en: Start from the middle mark, 3/6. See which way you have to move one gap to reach 4/6.

simpler.hi: Beech wala mark 3/6 hai, teen gap par. 2/6 ke liye do gap chalo toh tum beech se pehle rukte ho, aur 5/6 ke liye paanch gap chalo toh beech ke aage nikal jaate ho.
simpler.en: The middle mark is 3/6, three gaps along. Move two gaps for 2/6 and you stop before the middle; move five for 5/6 and you go past it.

problem.hi: Ek number line 0 se 1 tak hai. Is par 2/5 ka mark dhoondo.
problem.en: A number line runs from 0 to 1. Find the mark for 2/5.

problemAlt.hi: Socho 1 kilometre ki sadak hai, aur hume woh jagah dhoondni hai jo 2/5 kilometre par hai. Board ki line wahi sadak hai: 0 shuruaat, 1 aakhir.
problemAlt.en: Think of a 1 kilometre road where we must find the spot 2/5 kilometre along. The line on the board is that road: 0 is the start, 1 the end.

simpler.hi: Jaise pate ki do cheezein milkar ek hi ghar batati hain, waise hi 2/5 ke do number milkar line par ek jagah batate hain: neeche wala number gaps banata hai, upar wala number batata hai kitne chalne hain.
simpler.en: Just as two parts of an address together name one house, the two numbers of 2/5 together name one spot on the line: the bottom number makes the gaps, the top number says how many to move.

givens.hi: 2/5 mein neeche wala number 5, upar wala number 2
givens.en: 2/5 has bottom number 5 and top number 2

do.hi: Neeche wala number 5 dekho, aur 0 se 1 ko 5 barabar gaps mein kaato
do.en: Read the bottom number 5 and cut 0 to 1 into 5 equal gaps

why.hi: neeche wala number hi poore ke gaps ginta hai
why.en: the bottom number is the count of gaps in the whole

simpler.hi: Ek patti ko 5 barabar hisson mein kaatne ke liye 4 jagah kaatna padta hai. Line par bhi waise hi: 5 barabar gaps ke liye beech mein 4 marks.
simpler.en: To cut a strip into 5 equal parts you cut it in 4 places. The line is the same: 5 equal gaps need 4 marks in between.

do.hi: Ab dekho ek gap kitne ka hai
do.en: Now see what one gap is worth

why.hi: 5 barabar gaps milke 1 poora banate hain
why.en: 5 equal gaps together make 1 whole

simpler.hi: Ulta socho: ek gap ko 5 baar ek ke baad ek rakho, toh 0 se 1 poora bhar jaata hai. Isliye ek gap poore ka 1/5 hai.
simpler.en: Think of it backwards: lay one gap 5 times end to end and 0 to 1 is filled. So one gap is 1/5 of the whole.

prompt.hi: 2/5 ka upar wala number dekho: woh batata hai 0 se kitne gap chalna hai. Utne gap chalkar 0 ke baad kaunse mark par rukoge?
prompt.en: Look at the top number of 2/5: it says how many gaps to move from 0. Moving that many, which mark after 0 do you stop at?

reask.hi: 2/5 dikhane ke liye, 5 gaps wali is line par 0 ke baad kaunse mark par rukoge?
reask.en: To show 2/5 on this line of 5 gaps, which mark after 0 do you stop at?

why.hi: upar wala number 2 kehta hai 1/5 ke do gap chalo, isliye hum doosre mark par rukte hain
why.en: the top number 2 says take two gaps of 1/5, so we stop at the second mark

whyAlt.hi: mark ka naam 0 se gine gaps se aata hai, aur ginti 0 ke baad wale mark se shuru hoti hai: 1/5 wala mark pehla, 2/5 wala doosra
whyAlt.en: a mark's name comes from the gaps counted from 0, and the count starts at the mark after 0: the 1/5 mark is the first, the 2/5 mark the second

simpler.hi: 2/5 ka upar wala number 2 hai. 0 se ek-ek gap karke chalo, aur gino.
simpler.en: The top number of 2/5 is 2. Step from 0 one gap at a time, and count.

why.hi: upar wala number 2 kehta hai 0 se 1/5 ke 2 gap chalo
why.en: the top number 2 says move 2 gaps of 1/5 from 0

viewCaption.hi: Board par 0 se 1 tak ki line hai, paanch barabar gaps mein, aur beech mein chaar marks. 0 se shuru karke marks ko baari-baari dekho.
viewCaption.en: The board shows a line from 0 to 1, in five equal gaps, with four marks in between. Start at 0 and look at the marks in turn.

prompt.hi: 0 aur 1 ke beech 5 marks hain, sab barabar doori par. 0 ke baad chautha mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: There are 5 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1. What fraction is the 4th mark after 0?

did.hi: 5 marks wali line par chauthe mark ka fraction nikala
did.en: named the 4th mark's fraction on a line of 5 marks

viewCaption.hi: Yeh patti barabar hisson mein kati hai, aur baayein kinaare se kuch hisse rangin hain. Rang wahan khatam hota hai jahan line par chautha mark tha.
viewCaption.en: This strip is cut into equal parts, and some parts are coloured from the left end. The colour ends where the fourth mark was on the line.

why.hi: 5 marks se 6 barabar gaps bante hain, aur chautha mark 4 gaps par hai, yaani 4/6
why.en: 5 marks make 6 equal gaps, and the 4th mark is 4 gaps along, at 4/6

whyAlt.hi: board par seedha gino: 0 se 1 tak 6 gaps hain aur 0 se chauthe mark tak 4 gaps, toh 6 mein se 4, yaani 4/6
whyAlt.en: count straight off the board: 0 to 1 has 6 gaps and 0 to the 4th mark has 4, so 4 out of 6, that is 4/6

simpler.hi: Pehle gaps gino, woh marks se ek zyada hote hain. Phir 0 se chaar gap chalo.
simpler.en: First count the gaps, one more than the marks. Then walk four gaps from 0.

prompt.hi: Line ke upar wale gap 1/5 ke hain, line ke neeche wale 1/10 ke. 0 se chalte hue pehle kaun aata hai: 3/5 ya 3/10?
prompt.en: The gaps above the line are 1/5, the gaps below it 1/10. Walking from 0, which comes first: 3/5 or 3/10?

did.hi: 1/5 ke teen gap 1/10 ke teen gap se milaaye
did.en: set three gaps of 1/5 against three gaps of 1/10

viewCaption.hi: Do barabar lambi pattiyaan hain, pehli paanch barabar hisson mein, doosri das mein. Dono ke pehle teen hisse baayein kinaare se ek doosre ke saamne rakhkar dekho.
viewCaption.en: There are two strips of the same length, the first in five equal parts, the second in ten. Look at the first three parts of each, from the left end, side by side.

why.hi: 1/10 ka gap 1/5 ke gap ka aadha hai, toh 3 chhote gap 3/10 tak hi jaate hain, 3/5 se pehle
why.en: a 1/10 gap is half a 1/5 gap, so 3 short gaps reach only 3/10, before 3/5

whyAlt.hi: har 1/5 gap mein 1/10 ke do gap aate hain, toh 3/5 tak 1/10 ke 6 gap hain; 3/10 sirf 3 gap par hai, isliye pehle aata hai
whyAlt.en: each 1/5 gap holds two 1/10 gaps, so 3/5 is 6 gaps of 1/10; 3/10 is only 3 gaps along, so it comes first

simpler.hi: Dono taraf gap ki ginti barabar hai, bas lambai alag. 1/10 wala gap chhota hai ya 1/5 wala, yeh socho.
simpler.en: The gap count is the same on both sides, only the length differs. Think which gap is shorter, the 1/10 one or the 1/5 one.

prompt.hi: {friend} ka kehna hai ki 3/4 do number hain, 3 aur 4. 0 se 1 ki line par 3/4 dikhane ke liye kitne mark lagaoge: ek ya do?
prompt.en: {friend} says 3/4 is two numbers, 3 and 4. To show 3/4 on a 0-to-1 line, how many marks do you put: one or two?

did.hi: pehchaana ki 3/4 line par do nahi, ek hi jagah hai
did.en: saw that 3/4 is one place on the line, not two

viewCaption.hi: Board par 3/4 likha hai, aur uske saath 0 se 1 tak ki line chaar barabar gaps mein bati hai. Socho, 3/4 ka upar wala number aur neeche wala number is line par kya batate hain.
viewCaption.en: 3/4 is written on the board, and with it the line from 0 to 1 is split into four equal gaps. Think what the top number and the bottom number of 3/4 tell you on this line.

why.hi: 3/4 akela ek number hai, toh line par uski sirf ek jagah hai: 0 se 3 gap chalkar, wahi ek mark
why.en: 3/4 is a single number, so it has just one place on the line: 3 gaps on from 0, that one mark

whyAlt.hi: jaise ghar ka ek hi pata hota hai, waise hi line par 3/4 ki ek hi jagah hai; 3 aur 4 milkar us ek jagah ka naam batate hain
whyAlt.en: just as a house has one address, 3/4 has one place on the line; the 3 and the 4 together name that one place

simpler.hi: 3/4 ka neeche wala number 4 line ke barabar gaps banata hai, upar wala number 3 batata hai 0 se kitne gap chalna hai. Ab line par chalo aur gino tum kitni jagah ruke.
simpler.en: The bottom number 4 of 3/4 makes the line's equal gaps, and the top number 3 says how many gaps to walk from 0. Now walk the line and count how many places you stopped.

ladder.why: den 4: quarters already known from s1 and the c4 roti → carry a shaded 3 of 4 onto the line; top = gaps moved
den 3: before or after the middle with thirds → 1/3 before, 2/3 after; carries e3's middle test (sixths) to a den whose middle is not a mark
den 5 reversed: given the mark, name the fraction → 4/5 km; read the line instead of marking it
den 10: each fifth split in 2 → many small gaps, unit given as 1/10 km → 7 steps = 7/10
den 8 against den 4 → two different cuts, same stopping point (6/8 = 3/4); closes the loop back to quarters

remediation.move: marks to gaps on one line, quarters on top: 3 marks inside → 4 gaps, since there is a gap before the first mark and after the last (gaps = marks + 1); each gap = 1/4; 0 is the start, not a gap; 2 gaps → 2/4; then below: 9 marks → 10 gaps → one gap is 1/10 (the trap says 1/9). Not c1's case (5 marks, sixths)

say.hi: Marks ke beech ke gap dekho. Line ke upar 3 marks hain, par gap 4, kyunki pehle mark se pehle aur aakhri ke baad bhi ek-ek gap hai. Har gap 1/4. 0 se chalna shuru hota hai, aur 2 gap chalkar 2/4 aata hai.
say.en: Look at the gaps between the marks. Above the line there are 3 marks but 4 gaps, as there's a gap before the first mark and after the last. Each gap is 1/4. The walk starts at 0, and 2 gaps on is 2/4.

simpler.hi: Marks ko kainchi ke kat socho: 3 kat lagao toh ribbon ke 4 hisse bante hain. Line ke upar bhi 3 marks se 4 gap.
simpler.en: Think of the marks as scissor cuts: make 3 cuts and a ribbon falls into 4 pieces. Above the line too, 3 marks make 4 gaps.

sayAlt.hi: Chhota karke dekho: 0 aur 1 ke beech sirf 2 marks hon, toh gap 3 bante hain: 0 se pehle mark tak, phir doosre mark tak, phir 1 tak. Line ke upar bhi 3 marks ke 4 gap hain, isliye har gap 1/4.
sayAlt.en: Try it smaller: with just 2 marks between 0 and 1 there are 3 gaps: 0 to the first mark, then to the second, then to 1. Above the line too, 3 marks give 4 gaps, so each gap is 1/4.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti chaar barabar hisson mein hai, pehle do hisse rangin, 2/4, aur hisson ke beech teen marks. Doosri patti utni hi lambi hai, par uske hisse kaafi patle hain.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is in four equal parts, the first two coloured, 2/4, with three marks between the parts. The second strip is just as long, but its parts are much thinner.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche dekho: wahan 9 marks lage hain, sab barabar doori par. Wahan ek gap kitne ka hai?
prompt.en: Look below the line: there are 9 marks there, all evenly spaced. How much is one gap there?

reask.hi: Line ke neeche 9 barabar doori wale marks hon, toh ek gap kitne ka hai?
reask.en: If there are 9 evenly spaced marks below the line, how much is one gap?

viewCaption.hi: Doosri patti ke hisson ke beech ke marks hi line ke neeche wale marks hain, aur pehli patti mein chaar hisse hain, do rangin.
viewCaption.en: The marks between the second strip's parts are the marks below the line, and the first strip has four parts, two coloured.

why.hi: 9 marks se 10 barabar gaps bante hain, toh har gap 1/10
why.en: 9 marks make 10 equal gaps, so each gap is 1/10

whyAlt.hi: ek rassi ko 9 jagah kaato toh 10 barabar hisse bante hain, 9 nahi; line ke 9 marks bhi 10 gap banate hain, isliye ek gap 1/10 hai
whyAlt.en: cut a rope in 9 places and you get 10 equal pieces, not 9; the line's 9 marks make 10 gaps the same way, so one gap is 1/10

simpler.hi: Gap marks ke beech bhi hain aur dono siron par bhi. Pehle kul gap gino, phir socho ek gap kitne ka hai.
simpler.en: There are gaps between the marks and at both ends. First count all the gaps, then think what one gap is worth.

remediation.move: same number of hops, different hop size, on one 0-to-1 line, thirds on top, sixths below: a 1/3 hop is two 1/6 hops long; 2 hops of 1/6 stop at 2/6, 2 hops of 1/3 at 2/3 → bigger bottom number = shorter hops; then: 3 hops of 1/6 against 2/3

say.hi: Line ke upar aur neeche 0 se 2-2 gap chalo, par gap ki lambai alag hai. 1/3 ka gap 1/6 ke gap se do guna lamba hai. Toh 2 chhote gap 2/6 par rukte hain, aur 2 lambe gap 2/3 tak jaate hain.
say.en: Move 2 gaps from 0 above the line and below it, but the gaps differ in length. A 1/3 gap is twice a 1/6 gap. So 2 short gaps stop at 2/6, and 2 long gaps reach 2/3.

simpler.hi: Dono taraf do-do gap hain. 1/3 wala gap bada, toh 2/3 aage, aur 1/6 wala chhota, toh 2/6 peeche.
simpler.en: Two gaps each side. The 1/3 gap is bigger, so 2/3 is further on, and the 1/6 gap is smaller, so 2/6 stays back.

sayAlt.hi: Ek glass mein 2 bade chammach cheeni daalo, doosre mein 2 chhote chammach: ginti dono mein 2, par bade chammach wale mein zyada cheeni. Line par bhi 1/3 ke 2 lambe gap, 1/6 ke 2 chhote gap se aage pahunchte hain.
sayAlt.en: Put 2 big spoons of sugar in one glass and 2 small spoons in another: the count is 2 in both, but the big-spoon glass has more sugar. On the line too, 2 long gaps of 1/3 reach further than 2 short gaps of 1/6.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti ke do rangin hisse lambe hain, doosri ke do rangin hisse chhote. Dono mein rangin hisse do-do hain, par rang kahan tak pahuncha, woh alag hai.
viewCaption.en: The first strip's two coloured parts are long, the second strip's two coloured parts short. Both have two coloured parts, but how far the colour reaches is different.

prompt.hi: Line ke upar 1/3 ke 2 gap 2/3 tak gaye. Line ke neeche 1/6 ke 3 gap: woh 2/3 se pehle rukenge, ya baad mein?
prompt.en: Above the line, 2 gaps of 1/3 reached 2/3. Below the line, 3 gaps of 1/6: do they stop before 2/3, or after?

reask.hi: 1/6 ke 3 gap 0 se chalkar 2/3 se pehle rukenge, ya 2/3 ke baad?
reask.en: Do 3 gaps of 1/6 from 0 stop before 2/3, or after 2/3?

viewCaption.hi: Doosri patti chhe barabar hisson mein hai, aur uske do chhote hisse rangin hain; pehli mein teen mein se do lambe hisse rangin. Doosri patti ke hisse baayein kinaare se ek-ek karke pehli patti ke rang se milaao.
viewCaption.en: The second strip is in six equal parts, with two short parts coloured; the first has two of its three long parts coloured. Set the second strip's parts, one by one from the left end, against the colour of the first.

why.hi: 1/6 ke 3 gap sirf beech tak jaate hain, aur 2/3 beech se aage hai
why.en: 3 gaps of 1/6 reach only the middle, and 2/3 is past the middle

whyAlt.hi: 2/3 tak pahunchne ke liye 1/6 ke 4 gap chahiye, kyunki har 1/3 mein do 1/6 hain; 3 gap ek kam hai, toh pehle ruk jaate hain
whyAlt.en: reaching 2/3 takes 4 gaps of 1/6, since each 1/3 holds two 1/6; 3 gaps is one short, so they stop before

simpler.hi: Do chhote 1/6 gap milkar ek lamba 1/3 gap banate hain. 3 chhote gap, 2 lambe gap se kam padte hain.
simpler.en: Two short 1/6 gaps make one long 1/3 gap. 3 short gaps fall short of 2 long ones.

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (a 0-to-1 km line in eighths, the third stone marked), naming none of its numbers: each mark is a stone, one real spot of the road; wherever the toy stops it stands on one spot, so that spot has one number, a fraction, not two numbers; then the toy at the third stone → say it as one number, 3/8 km

say.hi: Line par har mark sadak ka ek patthar hai, ek pakki jagah. Ek chaabi wala khilona jis patthar par ruke, wahan uski ek hi jagah hai, toh number bhi ek hi: ek fraction, do alag number nahi.
say.en: Each mark on the line is a stone on the road, one real spot. Whichever stone a wind-up toy stops on, it is in one place, so it has one number: one fraction, not two separate numbers.

simpler.hi: Khilone ki jagah ko do number mein bolo toh lagta hai do jagah hain, par board par mark ek hi hai. Ek mark, ek naam.
simpler.en: Say the toy's spot as two numbers and it sounds like two places, but the board has only one mark. One mark, one name.

sayAlt.hi: Aadha kilo aata socho, yaani 1/2 kilo: likhne mein 1 aur 2 dono dikhte hain, par woh ek hi wazan hai. Har fraction aisa hi hai: ek number, aur line par uski ek hi jagah.
sayAlt.en: Think of half a kilo of flour, that is 1/2 kilo: written, it shows a 1 and a 2, but it is one weight. Every fraction is like that: one number, with one place on the line.

viewCaption.hi: Is patti ko sadak samjho: hisson ke beech ka har mark ek patthar hai. Rangin hissa sadak ke shuru se khilone ke patthar tak jaata hai.
viewCaption.en: Take this strip as the road: every mark between its parts is a stone. The coloured part runs from the start of the road to the toy's stone.

prompt.hi: Har 1/8 kilometre par patthar hai. Khilona teesre patthar par hai: board par us jagah ko ek number mein kaise likhoge?
prompt.en: A stone every 1/8 kilometre. The toy stands at the third stone: how do you write that spot on the board as one number?

reask.hi: Har 1/8 kilometre par patthar ho, toh 0 ke baad teesra patthar ek number mein kitne kilometre par hai?
reask.en: With a stone every 1/8 kilometre, at how many kilometres is the third stone after 0, as one number?

viewCaption.hi: Yeh wahi sadak hai: rang 0 se shuru hokar ek mark par rukta hai. Poori patti ke hisse bhi dekho aur rangin hisse bhi.
viewCaption.en: This is the same road: the colour starts at 0 and stops at one mark. Look at all the strip's parts, and at the coloured ones too.

why.hi: har patthar 1/8 kilometre aage hai, toh teesra patthar 3/8 kilometre par
why.en: each stone is 1/8 kilometre further on, so the third stone is at 3/8 kilometre

whyAlt.hi: 3 aur 8 alag-alag bolo toh do jagah ban jaati hain, par khilona ek hi patthar par hai; 8 mein se 3 gap, ek number, 3/8 kilometre
whyAlt.en: say 3 and 8 apart and you get two places, but the toy is on one stone; 3 gaps out of 8, one number, 3/8 kilometre

simpler.hi: Patthar se patthar 1/8 kilometre hai. Shuru se teesre patthar tak aise kitne gap hain, gino.
simpler.en: Stone to stone is 1/8 kilometre. Count how many of those gaps there are from the start to the third stone.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab fraction 1 ke aage bhi jaayenge: line kabhi 2 tak chalegi, kabhi 3 tak, aur dekhenge ki 1 se bade fraction kahan aate hain.
bridgeToNext.en: Next, fractions go past 1: the line will run to 2, sometimes to 3, and we'll see where fractions bigger than 1 sit.

simpler.hi: Ab line 1 ke aage bhi chalegi.
simpler.en: Now the line goes on past 1.

covered.hi: Phir fraction ka upar wala number aaya, jo batata hai ki 0 se kitne gap chalna hai, aur dono number milkar line ki ek hi jagah ka naam hote hain.
covered.en: Then came a fraction's top number, which says how many gaps to move from 0, and the two numbers together name one place on the line.

hook.convey: one whole is finished and the mover keeps going → the stopping point is past 1 → it needs a fraction name bigger than 1 → the line must go on beyond 1

use.hi: Cricket mein ek run matlab pitch ki poori lambai, yaani 1. Batsman ek run pura karke doosre ke liye bhaaga, aur aadhi pitch par ruk gaya. Woh 1 se aage hai, toh uska fraction bhi 1 se bada hoga.
use.en: In cricket one run is the full length of the pitch, that is 1. The batsman finishes one run, sets off on a second, and stops halfway. He's past 1, so his fraction is bigger than 1.

use.hi: Train station 0 se chali, station 1 paar kiya, aur station 2 se pehle raaste mein ruk gayi. Woh jagah 1 ke aage hai, toh us jagah ka number bhi 1 se bada hoga.
use.en: A train leaves station 0, passes station 1, and stops before station 2. That spot is past 1, so the spot's number is bigger than 1 too.

explain.convey: the line does not stop at 1 → it carries on to 2; the second whole is cut the same way → 4 equal gaps per whole, all the same size; 4 gaps from 0 = 4/4 = 1; the gap count from 0 keeps growing past 4

viewCaption.hi: Board par line 1 ke aage bhi chalti hai, aur har poore mein chaar barabar gaps hain. 1 wale mark par 4/4 = 1 likha hai, aur uske aage bhi gaps usi lambai ke hain.
viewCaption.en: The board's line carries on past 1, with four equal gaps in each whole. The mark at 1 reads 4/4 = 1, and the gaps after it are the same length.

point.hi: Yeh rahi 0 se 2 tak ki line. Har poore ke 4 barabar gaps hain, aur 1 wala mark hai 4/4, yaani 4/4 = 1. 1 ke aage bhi gaps usi size mein chalte rehte hain.
point.en: Here is a line from 0 to 2. Each whole has 4 equal gaps, and the mark at 1 is 4/4, so 4/4 = 1. Beyond 1 the gaps keep going, same size.

pointAlt.hi: Apna ruler dekho: woh 1 cm par khatam nahi hota, 2, 3, aage 15 cm tak chalta hai. Number line bhi waise hi 1 ke baad chalti rehti hai, aur wahan bhi har poore mein 4 barabar gaps hain.
pointAlt.en: Look at your ruler: it doesn't end at 1 cm, it goes on to 2, 3, all the way to 15 cm. The number line carries on after 1 the same way, and there too each whole has 4 equal gaps.

prompt.hi: 1/5 wale gaps ab line ke neeche hain. 0 se 6 gap chalo. 1 se pehle rukoge, ya 1 ke baad?
prompt.en: The gaps of 1/5 are now below the line. Move 6 gaps from 0. Do you stop before 1, or after?

reask.hi: Har gap 1/5 ka ho, toh 0 se 6 gap chalkar 1 se pehle rukoge, ya 1 ke baad?
reask.en: If each gap is 1/5, after 6 gaps from 0 do you stop before 1, or after 1?

why.hi: 5 gap se 5/5 = 1 aa gaya, toh chhatha gap 1 ke baad, 6/5 par
why.en: 5 gaps already make 5/5 = 1, so the 6th gap lands after 1, at 6/5

whyAlt.hi: 5 barabar hisson wale ek pizza se 6 hisse nahi nikalte, doosra pizza kholna padta hai; waise hi 1/5 ke 6 gap ek poore se ek gap aage jaate hain
whyAlt.en: a pizza in 5 equal parts can't give 6 parts, you have to open a second one; just so, 6 gaps of 1/5 go one gap past a whole

simpler.hi: 1/5 wale gaps par 0 se gino, aur dekho ki 1 tak pahunchne mein kitne gap lagte hain.
simpler.en: Count along the gaps of 1/5 from 0, and see how many gaps it takes to reach 1.

viewCaption.hi: Ab line ke dono taraf gaps hain: line ke upar har poore mein chaar, line ke neeche paanch. Line ke neeche wale gaps 0 se ek-ek karke dekho, aur 1 wala mark dhyan mein rakho.
viewCaption.en: Now there are gaps on both sides of the line: four in each whole above it, five below it. Look along the gaps below the line one by one from 0, and keep the mark at 1 in mind.

simpler.hi: 1 se 2 tak ka hissa bhi 0 se 1 jitna hi lamba hai, aur usmein bhi utne hi gap hain.
simpler.en: The stretch from 1 to 2 is just as long as 0 to 1, and it has just as many gaps.

explain.convey: 6 hops of 1/4 from 0: the first 4 hops fill one whole → reach 1; 2 more hops → past 1 → 6/4 = 1 and 2/4; top > bottom → beyond 1

viewCaption.hi: Line par 0 se gap-gap karke chalne ke teer bane hain, jo 6/4 wale mark par rukte hain. Raaste mein 1 wala mark beech mein aata hai.
viewCaption.en: The line has arrows going gap by gap from 0, and they stop at the 6/4 mark. The mark at 1 comes along the way.

point.hi: Line par har gap 1/4 hai. 0 se 6 gap chalo: pehle 4 gap 1 tak, phir do gap aur, aur hum 6/4 par, 1 ke aage. 6/4 ka upar wala number 6, 4 se bada hai, isliye hum 1 ke aage nikal gaye.
point.en: On the line each gap is 1/4. Move 6 gaps from 0: the first 4 reach 1, then two more, and we're at 6/4, past 1. 6/4's top number 6 is bigger than 4, so we went past 1.

pointAlt.hi: Ek jug mein 4 glass paani aata hai: 6 glass daalo toh ek jug bhar jaata hai aur 2 glass doosre jug mein jaate hain. 6/4 bhi aisa hi hai: ek poora, aur uske aage 2/4.
pointAlt.en: A jug holds 4 glasses of water: pour in 6 glasses and one jug fills, and 2 glasses go into a second jug. 6/4 is like that: one whole, and 2/4 past it.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche har gap 1/2 ka hai. 0 se aise 4 gap chalkar line ke kis number tak pahunchoge?
prompt.en: Below the line each gap is 1/2. Moving 4 such gaps from 0, which number on the line do you reach?

reask.hi: 1/2 wale 4 gap 0 se chalkar line ke kis number tak pahunchoge?
reask.en: Moving 4 gaps of 1/2 from 0, which number on the line do you reach?

why.hi: 4/2 matlab 1/2 ke 4 gap, aur har 2 gap se ek poora banta hai, toh 4/2 = 2
why.en: 4/2 is 4 gaps of 1/2, and every 2 gaps make one whole, so 4/2 = 2

whyAlt.hi: 2 aadhi rotiyan milkar ek poori roti; 4 aadhi rotiyan, toh 2 poori rotiyan, isliye 4/2 = 2
whyAlt.en: 2 half rotis make one whole roti; 4 halves make 2 whole rotis, so 4/2 = 2

simpler.hi: Do aadhe milkar ek poora banate hain. 1/2 wale gaps ko do-do karke gino.
simpler.en: Two halves make one whole. Count the gaps of 1/2 in twos.

viewCaption.hi: Line ke neeche wale gaps lambe hain, har poore mein sirf do. Line ke upar 6/4 wala mark ab bhi dikh raha hai.
viewCaption.en: The gaps below the line are long, only two in each whole. The 6/4 mark above the line is still showing.

simpler.hi: Chaar chauthai milkar ek poora banta hai. 6 chauthai mein ek poora bhi hai, aur do chauthai usse aage.
simpler.en: Four quarters make one whole. Six quarters hold one whole, and two quarters more beyond it.

explain.convey: thirds on a line to 3: every 3 gaps = one whole → 3/3 = 1; group the gaps in threes to find which wholes a fraction has passed; top above 3 → past 1

viewCaption.hi: Is board par teen poore ek ke baad ek rakhe hain, har ek teen barabar gaps mein. Pehle teen gaps ke end par 3/3 = 1 likha hai.
viewCaption.en: This board lays three wholes end to end, each in three equal gaps. At the end of the first three gaps it reads 3/3 = 1.

point.hi: Yeh line 0 se 3 tak hai, har poore ke 3 barabar gaps. Pehle teen gaps 1 par khatam hote hain, wahan 3/3 = 1. Teen-teen gaps ka ek group, aur har group ek poora.
point.en: This line runs from 0 to 3, each whole in 3 equal gaps. The first three gaps end at 1, where it says 3/3 = 1. Take the gaps in groups of three gaps; each group is one whole.

pointAlt.hi: Laddu ginte waqt hum unhe teen-teen ke group mein rakhte hain. Is line ke gaps bhi waise hi gino: har 3 gaps ka group ek poora hai, isliye pehle group ke end par 1 hai.
pointAlt.en: When counting laddoos we put them in groups of three. Count this line's gaps the same way: each group of 3 gaps is one whole, so 1 is at the end of the first group.

prompt.hi: 7/3 ke 7 gaps ko teen-teen ke group mein rakho. Har group mein theek teen gap hon, toh kitne group bante hain?
prompt.en: Put the 7 gaps of 7/3 in threes. If each group has exactly three gaps, how many groups do you get?

reask.hi: 7/3 ke 7 gaps mein theek teen-teen gaps wale kitne group bante hain?
reask.en: How many groups of exactly three gaps are in the 7 gaps of 7/3?

why.hi: 7/3 ke 7 gaps mein teen-teen gaps ke 2 group bante hain, 6/3 = 2, aur 1 gap bachta hai
why.en: 7/3 has 7 gaps: 2 groups of three gaps, 6/3 = 2, and 1 gap left over

whyAlt.hi: 7 laddu teen-teen karke rakho: 3, phir 3, aur 1 bacha; teen wale 2 group, isliye 7/3, 2 ke aage hai
whyAlt.en: set 7 laddoos out in threes: 3, then 3, and 1 left; 2 groups of three, so 7/3 is past 2

simpler.hi: Saat gaps ko teen-teen ke group mein rakhte jao. Jo gap akela bach jaaye, woh group nahi banata.
simpler.en: Keep putting the seven gaps into groups of three. A gap left on its own does not make a group.

simpler.hi: Teen gap chalo toh 1 aata hai, teen aur chalo toh agla poora number. Har poora number pichhle se teen gap aage hai.
simpler.en: Move three gaps and you reach 1; three more and you reach the next whole number. Each whole number is three gaps past the one before.

problem.hi: Ek number line 0 se 2 tak hai. Is par 7/4 ka mark dhoondo.
problem.en: A number line runs from 0 to 2. Find the mark for 7/4.

problemAlt.hi: Ek cycle race 0 se 2 kilometre ki hai, aur ek cycle 7/4 kilometre chalkar ruki. Board ki line par uski jagah dhoondni hai.
problemAlt.en: A cycle race runs from 0 to 2 kilometres, and a cycle stops after 7/4 kilometre. We need its spot on the board's line.

simpler.hi: Chauthai rotiyaan gino: 4 chauthai milkar ek poori roti banti hai, aur 7 chauthai usse zyada hain. Isliye 7/4 ek poore se aage jaayega, aur line 1 par nahi, 2 tak chahiye.
simpler.en: Count quarter rotis: 4 quarters make one whole roti, and 7 quarters are more than that. So 7/4 goes past one whole, and the line has to reach 2, not stop at 1.

givens.hi: 7/4 mein neeche wala number 4, upar wala number 7
givens.en: 7/4 has bottom number 4 and top number 7

do.hi: Line par 0, 1 aur 2 likho, aur har poore ke 4 barabar gaps karo
do.en: Write 0, 1 and 2 on the line, and cut each whole into 4 equal gaps

steps.result: 0 se 2 tak kul 8 bane, har ek 1/4 ka

why.hi: neeche wala number 4 hai, aur 7/4 ko 1 ke aage jaana hai
why.en: the bottom number is 4, and 7/4 has to go past 1

simpler.hi: Do pizza socho, dono 4 barabar hisson mein kate hue: kul 8 hisse, aur har hissa ek pizza ka 1/4. Line ke do poore bhi aise hi 8 gaps mein bat jaate hain.
simpler.en: Picture two pizzas, each cut into 4 equal parts: 8 parts in all, and each part is 1/4 of a pizza. The line's two wholes split into 8 gaps the same way.

do.hi: Upar wala number 7 matlab 7 gap chalna hai, toh pehle 4 gap chalo
do.en: The top number 7 means 7 gaps to move, so first move 4

why.hi: ek poore mein 4 gap hote hain, aur humein usse zyada, 7 gap chalne hain
why.en: one whole holds 4 gaps, and we have more than that, 7 gaps, to move

simpler.hi: Ek seedhi socho jisme har 4 paydaan par ek manzil aati hai. 7 paydaan chadhne hain, toh pehle 4 paydaan par tum pehli manzil par ho; line par woh manzil 1 hai.
simpler.en: Picture stairs with a floor after every 4 steps. You have 7 steps to climb, so after the first 4 you are at the first floor; on the line that floor is 1.

prompt.hi: Kul 7 gap chalne the, aur 4 gap mein hum 1 tak aa gaye. 1 ke baad aur kitne gap bache?
prompt.en: We had 7 gaps to move, and 4 got us to 1. How many more are left after 1?

reask.hi: 7 gap mein se 4 gap chalkar 1 aa gaya, toh 1 ke baad kitne gap bache?
reask.en: Of 7 gaps, 4 got us to 1; how many gaps are left after 1?

why.hi: 7 mein se 4 gap chal kar hum 1 par pahunche, aur 7 − 4 = 3 gap bache
why.en: 4 of the 7 gaps took us to 1, and 7 − 4 = 3 gaps are left

whyAlt.hi: 1 ke baad ek-ek gap gino aur 7/4 par ruko: ek, do, teen; yaani teen gap aur
whyAlt.en: count gaps one at a time after 1 and stop at 7/4: one, two, three; that is three more gaps

simpler.hi: Kul 7 the, 4 ho gaye. Baaki nikalne ke liye 7 mein se 4 ghatao.
simpler.en: 7 in all, 4 done. Take 4 away from 7 to get the rest.

answer.hi: 7/4, 1 ke baad teesra mark hai, yaani 1 aur 3/4, 2 se bas ek gap pehle
answer.en: 7/4 is the 3rd mark after 1, that is 1 and 3/4, just one gap before 2

why.hi: 7 = 4 + 3: pehle 4 gap se 1 poora hua, baaki 3 gap 1 ke aage gaye
why.en: 7 = 4 + 3: the first 4 gaps make 1 whole, the other 3 go past 1

viewCaption.hi: Is line par kul aath barabar gaps hain, aur 0, 1 aur 2 line ke neeche likhe hain. Line ke upar 7/4 likha hai, jiski jagah dhoondni hai.
viewCaption.en: This line has eight equal gaps in all, with 0, 1 and 2 written below it. Above the line is 7/4, whose spot we are finding.

prompt.hi: Ek line lo, 0 se 2 tak, har poora 3 barabar gaps mein. 5/3 kaun se do numbers ke beech aata hai: 0 aur 1, ya 1 aur 2?
prompt.en: Take a line from 0 to 2, each whole in 3 equal gaps. Between which two numbers is 5/3: 0 and 1, or 1 and 2?

did.hi: teen-teen gaps ke group banakar 5/3 ki jagah dhoondhi
did.en: grouped the gaps in threes to find where 5/3 sits

viewCaption.hi: Board par 5/3 likha hai. Line par 0 se gap gino: har teen gap ke baad ek poora number aata hai, pehle 1, phir 2.
viewCaption.en: 5/3 is written on the board. Count gaps along the line from 0: after every three gaps comes a whole number, first 1, then 2.

why.hi: 3/3 = 1 aur 6/3 = 2, aur 5/3 dono ke beech hai
why.en: 3/3 = 1 and 6/3 = 2, and 5/3 sits between them

whyAlt.hi: 5/3 ke 5 gap mein se pehle 3 gap 1 tak le jaate hain, aur bache 2 gap ek aur poora nahi banate, toh woh 1 aur 2 ke beech rukta hai
whyAlt.en: of 5/3's 5 gaps, the first 3 take you to 1, and the 2 left don't make another whole, so it stops between 1 and 2

simpler.hi: 3 gaps milke ek poora banate hain. 5/3 ke gaps mein se pehle 3 tumhe 0 se ek poore tak le jaate hain; ab socho baaki gap kis taraf jaate hain.
simpler.en: 3 gaps together make one whole. Of the gaps in 5/3, the first 3 take you from 0 to one whole; now think which way the rest go.

prompt.hi: Line 0 se 2 tak. 1/6 ke 11 gap chalo, ya 1/12 ke 11 gap. 0 se zyada door kaun gaya: 11/6 ya 11/12?
prompt.en: A line from 0 to 2. Move 11 gaps of 1/6, or 11 gaps of 1/12. Which goes further from 0: 11/6 or 11/12?

did.hi: 1/6 aur 1/12 ke 11-11 gap chalkar dekha kaun aage gaya
did.en: walked 11 gaps of 1/6 and of 1/12 to compare them

viewCaption.hi: Line ke upar har poore mein chhe gaps hain, line ke neeche barah, aur dono taraf ke gaps 0 se shuru hote hain.
viewCaption.en: Above the line there are six gaps in each whole, below it twelve, and the gaps on both sides start at 0.

why.hi: 1/6 ka gap 1/12 ke gap se do guna hai, toh 11 lambe gap 11/6 tak, 11/12 se kaafi aage
why.en: a 1/6 gap is twice a 1/12 gap, so 11 long gaps reach 11/6, well past 11/12

whyAlt.hi: 11/12 mein upar wala number 11 neeche wale number 12 se chhota hai, toh woh 1 se pehle; 11/6 mein upar wala number 11 neeche wale number 6 se bada hai, toh woh 1 ke aage, isliye 11/6 door hai
whyAlt.en: in 11/12 the top number 11 is smaller than the bottom number 12, so it's before 1; in 11/6 the top number 11 is bigger than the bottom number 6, so it's past 1, which makes 11/6 further

simpler.hi: Gap dono taraf 11 hain. Lamba gap kaunsa hai, 1/6 wala ya 1/12 wala, bas yeh socho.
simpler.en: 11 gaps on each side. Just think which gap is longer, the 1/6 one or the 1/12 one.

prompt.hi: Is line par 0, 1, 2 aur 3 likhe hain, aur har do poore numbers ke beech 5 barabar gaps hain. 2 ke baad doosra mark kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: This line has 0, 1, 2 and 3 written on it, with 5 equal gaps between each pair of whole numbers. What fraction is the 2nd mark after 2?

did.hi: 0 se gaps ginkar 2 ke baad doosre mark ka naam rakha
did.en: counted the gaps from 0 and named the second mark after 2

viewCaption.hi: Line par 2 ke aage ek mark alag se dikhaya gaya hai: wahi jagah dhoondni hai. Har gap ki lambai poori line par ek jaisi hai.
viewCaption.en: Past 2 on the line, one mark is shown apart from the rest: that is the spot to find. Every gap is the same length all along the line.

why.hi: har 5 gaps se ek poora, toh 2 tak 10 gaps hain; 2 gap aur chalo toh kul 12, yaani 12/5
why.en: every 5 gaps make one whole, so 2 is 10 gaps from 0; 2 more gaps make 12, so 12/5

whyAlt.hi: 12 gaps ko paanch-paanch karke gino: 5, phir 5, aur 2 bache; yaani 2 poore aur 2 gap, jo 2 ke baad doosra mark hai, isliye 12/5
whyAlt.en: count 12 gaps in fives: 5, then 5, and 2 left; that is 2 wholes and 2 gaps, the 2nd mark after 2, so 12/5

simpler.hi: Pehle gino 0 se 2 tak kitne gaps hain, phir usme 2 aur jodo. Wahi kul ginti fraction ka upar wala number hai.
simpler.en: First count the gaps from 0 to 2, then add 2 more. That total is the fraction's top number.

ladder.why: den 4 on 0 to 2, same den and line as e1, e2 and the worked example → 5/4 = one quarter past 1; smallest step beyond 1
den 3, no line given → decide before/after 1 from top vs bottom alone (4 > 3); moves the rule off the picture
den 2 inside a story: 1 km + half km → count in halves → 3/2; build the improper fraction from a real distance

remediation.move: eighth-gaps laid end to end on a 0-to-2 line, no squeezing: 8 gaps fill 0 to 1 exactly → 1 is full → the 9th gap must go past 1; then below, each whole in sixths: a runner runs 7 gaps → 7/6; a fraction is a length, and lengths can exceed one whole

say.hi: Line 0 se 2 tak hai, line ke upar har gap 1/8 ka. 8 gap 0 se 1 tak ki saari jagah bhar dete hain, isliye 1 wala mark 8/8 hai. Naunve gap ki jagah andar nahi bachi, toh woh 1 ke aage hai.
say.en: The line runs from 0 to 2, each gap above it 1/8. The first 8 gaps fill all the room from 0 to 1, so the mark at 1 is 8/8. No room is left inside for the ninth gap, so it is past 1.

simpler.hi: Ek bench par aath bachchon ki jagah ho aur nau bachche aayein, toh naunve ko doosri bench par baithna padta hai. Naunva gap bhi aise hi 1 ke aage jaata hai.
simpler.en: If a bench has room for eight children and nine come, the ninth has to sit on a second bench. The ninth gap goes past 1 the same way.

sayAlt.hi: 1 se peeche ki taraf dekho: 1 par 8/8 hai, aur usse ek gap peeche 7/8. Ginti 8 se jitni aage badhti hai, gap utne hi 1 ke paar jaate hain, jaise naunva gap 9/8 par.
sayAlt.en: Look back from 1: 8/8 is at 1, and one gap back is 7/8. However far the count goes past 8, that many gaps go past 1, like the ninth gap at 9/8.

viewCaption.hi: Line ke upar har gap 1/8 ka hai, aur 8/8 wala mark theek 1 par hai. Line ke neeche har poora chhe barabar gaps mein hai.
viewCaption.en: Above the line each gap is 1/8, and the 8/8 mark sits exactly on 1. Below the line each whole is in six equal gaps.

prompt.hi: Line ke neeche har poora 6 barabar gaps mein hai. Ek runner 0 se 7 gap daudta hai. Woh kis fraction par rukta hai?
prompt.en: Below the line each whole is in 6 equal gaps. A runner runs 7 gaps from 0. What fraction does the runner stop on?

reask.hi: Har poora 6 barabar gaps mein ho, toh 0 se 7 gap daudkar runner kis fraction par rukta hai?
reask.en: If each whole is in 6 equal gaps, what fraction does a runner stop on after 7 gaps from 0?

viewCaption.hi: Line ke neeche dekho: 1 tak ke gap aur 1 ke baad ke gap. Line ke upar wala 8/8 ka mark dikhata hai ki 1 kahan hai.
viewCaption.en: Look below the line: the gaps up to 1 and the gaps after 1. The 8/8 mark above the line shows where 1 is.

why.hi: har gap 1/6 hai, aur runner ne 7 gap daude, toh 7/6
why.en: each gap is 1/6 and the runner ran 7 gaps, so 7/6

whyAlt.hi: 6/6 par runner 1 tak pahunch gaya, par ruka nahi, ek gap aur daudha; isliye woh 1 ke aage, 7/6 par hai
whyAlt.en: at 6/6 the runner reached 1 but didn't stop, running one more gap; so the runner is past 1, at 7/6

simpler.hi: Ek poore mein 6 gaps hain, aur runner ne 7 gap daude. Inhi do gintiyon se fraction banta hai.
simpler.en: One whole has 6 gaps, and the runner ran 7 gaps. The fraction is made from these two counts.

remediation.move: on the then-card's own board (a 0-to-2 line, fifths on top, tenths below), naming none of its numbers: same top number → same gap count; a bigger bottom number → shorter gaps → the same number of gaps stops sooner; then the child says which of 9/5 and 9/10 is past 1

say.hi: Jab do fractions ka upar wala number ek jaisa ho, toh dono mein utne hi gap chalne hain; farak gap ki lambai ka hai. Neeche wala number bada ho, toh har gap chhota, aur utne hi gap jaldi khatam ho jaate hain.
say.en: When two fractions have the same top number, both move the same number of gaps; only the gap length differs. A bigger bottom number makes each gap shorter, so the same number of gaps ends sooner.

simpler.hi: Dono mein gap ki ginti ek hai. Bas socho, jis taraf ek poore mein kam gaps hain, wahan ek gap lamba hota hai.
simpler.en: The gap count is the same. Just think: on the side with fewer gaps in one whole, each gap is longer.

sayAlt.hi: Do trainon mein 3-3 dibbe hain, ek ke dibbe lambe, ek ke chhote: ginti barabar, par lambe dibbon wali train zyada lambi hai. Fraction mein bhi upar wala number ek ho, toh jiska neeche wala number chhota, uske gap lambe, aur woh aage pahunchta hai.
sayAlt.en: Two trains have 3 coaches each, one with long coaches, one with short: the count is the same, but the long-coach train is longer. With fractions too, when the top numbers match, the one with the smaller bottom number has longer gaps and reaches further.

prompt.hi: Nayi line, 0 se 2: ek taraf har poora 5 gaps mein, doosri taraf 10 mein. Kaun 1 ke aage hai: 9/5 ya 9/10?
prompt.en: A new line, 0 to 2: on one side each whole is in 5 gaps, on the other in 10. Which is past 1: 9/5 or 9/10?

viewCaption.hi: Ek hi line hai, 0 se 2 tak: paanch-paanch gaps wale poore line ke upar, das-das wale line ke neeche, aur beech mein 1 wala mark.
viewCaption.en: There is just one line, 0 to 2: wholes of five gaps above it, wholes of ten below it, and the mark at 1 in between.

why.hi: dono mein 9 gap, par 1/5 wala gap do guna lamba: 9/5, 1 ke aage hai, aur 9/10, 1 se pehle
why.en: both are 9 gaps, but a 1/5 gap is twice a 1/10 gap: 9/5 is past 1, 9/10 before 1

whyAlt.hi: 9/10 toh 1 tak bhi nahi pahunchta, par 9/5 mein pehle 5 gap se hi 1 aa jaata hai aur 4 gap aur bachte hain
whyAlt.en: 9/10 never even reaches 1, but in 9/5 the first 5 gaps already reach 1 and 4 more are left

simpler.hi: Har fraction ka upar wala number uske neeche wale number se milakar dekho. Upar wala number bada ho, toh fraction 1 ke aage hota hai.
simpler.en: Set each fraction's top number against its bottom number. If the top number is bigger, the fraction is past 1.

remediation.move: train between stations, on the then-card's own board (stations 0, 1, 2, each stretch in 5 equal parts): station 1 = 5/5; wherever the train halts is one real spot on the track with one number: the parts counted from 0, over 5; then a train from station 1 that goes 3 parts on

say.hi: Yeh stations ki line hai, 0 se 2. Do stations ke beech 5 barabar gaps hain, toh station 1 ki jagah 5/5 hai. Train jahan ruke, woh ek pakki jagah hai, aur uska ek hi number: 0 se gine hue gap, bata 5.
say.en: This is a line of stations, 0 to 2. Between two stations there are 5 equal gaps, so station 1 sits at 5/5. Wherever the train stops is one real spot, and that spot has one number: the gaps counted from 0, over 5.

simpler.hi: Station 1 ke aage bhi gap 0 se hi gine jaate hain, ginti 1 par rukti nahi. Isliye 1 ke baad wale mark ka upar wala number 5 se bada hota hai.
simpler.en: Past station 1 the gaps are still counted from 0; the count does not stop at 1. So a mark after 1 has a top number bigger than 5.

sayAlt.hi: Chhoti line socho, 0 se 1, sirf 2 barabar gaps: beech ka mark ek hi jagah hai, aur uska naam ek hi number hai, 1/2. Stations ki line par bhi train jahan ruke, uska naam ek fraction hai, do alag number nahi.
sayAlt.en: Picture a small line, 0 to 1, with just 2 equal gaps: the middle mark is one place, and its name is one number, 1/2. On the line of stations too, wherever the train stops, its name is one fraction, not two separate numbers.

viewCaption.hi: Yeh stations ki line hai: 0, 1 aur 2 par stations, aur har do stations ke beech paanch barabar gaps. Ek mark station 1 ke aage hai, jahan train ruki.
viewCaption.en: This is the line of stations: stations at 0, 1 and 2, with five equal gaps between each pair. One mark sits past station 1, where the train stopped.

prompt.hi: Isi 0 se 2 ki line par ek doosri train station 1 se chali aur 3 gap aage ruki. Woh kis fraction par khadi hai?
prompt.en: On this line from 0 to 2, another train starts at station 1 and stops 3 gaps on. What fraction is it standing on?

reask.hi: Station 1 se 3 gap aage rukne wali train kis fraction par khadi hai?
reask.en: A train that stops 3 gaps past station 1 stands on what fraction?

viewCaption.hi: Board par stations ki line 0 se 2 tak hai, aur station 1 par paanch gaps poore hote hain. Station 1 ke aage wala mark train ki jagah hai.
viewCaption.en: The board's line of stations runs from 0 to 2, and five gaps are complete at station 1. The mark past station 1 is the train's spot.

why.hi: station 1 = 5/5 hai, aur 3 gap aage 5 + 3 = 8, yaani 8/5
why.en: station 1 is 5/5, and 3 gaps on makes 5 + 3 = 8 gaps, that is 8/5

whyAlt.hi: station 2 se ulta gino: 2 = 10/5, aur train usse 2 gap pehle hai, toh 8/5
whyAlt.en: count back from station 2: 2 is 10/5, and the train is 2 gaps before it, so 8/5

simpler.hi: 1 tak pahunchne mein jitne gap lage, usme 3 aur jodo. Yahi jod fraction ka upar wala number hai.
simpler.en: Take the gaps it takes to reach 1 and add 3 more. That sum is the fraction's top number.

covered.hi: Aakhir mein line 1 ke aage chali, aur jab upar wala number neeche wale number se bada ho, toh fraction 1 ke aage aata hai.
covered.en: Last, the line went on past 1, and when the top number is bigger than the bottom number, the fraction comes after 1.

prompt.hi: Ek line 0 se 2 tak hai. 0 aur 1 ke beech 6 marks hain, aur 1 aur 2 ke beech bhi 6, sab barabar doori par. 0 se 9 gap chalo toh kis fraction par pahunchoge?
prompt.en: A line runs from 0 to 2. There are 6 evenly spaced marks between 0 and 1, and 6 more between 1 and 2. Which fraction do you reach after moving 9 gaps from 0?

did.hi: 6 marks se gap nikala aur 0 se 9 gap gine
did.en: found each gap from 6 marks and counted 9 gaps from 0

why.hi: 6 marks se har poore ke 7 barabar gaps bante hain, toh har gap 1/7; 0 se 9 gap chalkar 9/7 aata hai, jo 1 ke aage hai.
why.en: 6 marks make 7 equal gaps in each whole, so each gap is 1/7; 9 gaps from 0 reach 9/7, which is past 1.

viewCaption.hi: Is line par 0 se 1 tak aur 1 se 2 tak, dono poore ek jaise gaps mein kate hain. Ungli 0 par rakho aur gaps ek-ek karke gino.
viewCaption.en: On this line, 0 to 1 and 1 to 2 are both cut into the same gaps. Put a finger on 0 and count the gaps one by one.

covered.hi: Aaj ki baat yeh thi ki har fraction ki number line par ek pakki jagah hoti hai: neeche wala number 0 se 1 ke barabar gaps ginta hai, aur upar wala number batata hai 0 se kitne gap chalna hai. Jab upar wala number neeche wale number se bada ho, toh fraction 1 ke aage aata hai.
covered.en: Today was about every fraction having its own place on the number line: the bottom number counts the equal gaps from 0 to 1, and the top number says how many gaps to move from 0. When the top number is bigger than the bottom number, the fraction comes after 1.
